title: Getting Started with QuantLib in Python
text: QuantLib is the most comprehensive open-source library for quantitative finance. It handles everything from date arithmetic to full term structure models and derivatives pricing. This post walks through the basics.

title: Getting Started with QuantLib in Python
text:
Setup
If you’re using the fineng conda environment:
conda install -c conda-forge quantlib-python
Then import:
import QuantLib as ql
print(ql.__version__)

title: Getting Started with QuantLib in Python
text:
Setting the evaluation date
QuantLib has a global evaluation date that anchors all calculations:
today = ql.Date(14, 3, 2026)
ql.Settings.instance().evaluationDate = today
print(f"Evaluation date: {today}")

title: Getting Started with QuantLib in Python
text:
Building a discount curve
A discount curve maps each future date to a discount factor \(P(0, T)\), which represents the present value of 1 unit of currency received at time \(T\).
\[P(0, T) = e^{-r(T) \cdot T}\]
dates = [
    today,
    today + ql.Period(6, ql.Months),
    today + ql.Period(1, ql.Years),
    today + ql.Period(2, ql.Years),
    today + ql.Period(5, ql.Years),
    today + ql.Period(10, ql.Years),
]

discounts = [1.0, 0.978, 0.955, 0.910, 0.820, 0.680]

curve = ql.DiscountCurve(dates, discounts, ql.Actual360())
curve.enableExtrapolation()

# Query the curve
print(f"1Y discount  : {curve.discount(today + ql.Period(1, ql.Years)):.4f}")
print(f"5Y discount  : {curve.discount(today + ql.Period(5, ql.Years)):.4f}")
print(f"10Y zero rate: {curve.zeroRate(10.0, ql.Continuous).rate():.4%}")

title: Hello World — Why I Started This Blog
text: After years of scribbling notes into private notebooks and Jupyter cells, I decided it was time to write in public.

title: Hello World — Why I Started This Blog
text:
Who I am
I’m a financial engineer at PSP Investments in Montreal. My day-to-day involves quantitative modelling in credit risk and derivatives — building tools that help understand complex financial exposures across a large institutional portfolio.
Outside the office, I’ve been steadily building skills in machine learning and modern data science, completing certifications in deep learning, TensorFlow, and Python data science. I’ve also started experimenting with Julia, which I’m genuinely excited about for numerical computing.

title: Hello World — Why I Started This Blog
text:
What I’ll write about
A mix of things:

Quantitative finance — yield curves, derivatives pricing, counterparty credit risk
QuantLib — practical guides to using QuantLib in Python
Machine learning in finance — applying ML to financial problems
Julia — numerical computing experiments
Tools and workflow — how I set up and run my development environment

Some posts will be regular markdown. Others will be Jupyter notebooks rendered directly — so you’ll see live code output alongside the writing.
